rationale: One major finding: the description field in both the Python constant and the YAML entry says 'Schedulers navigation item and REST API for listing, toggling, and viewing run history' — implying the flag gates API access — but no router guard is implemented. The implementation is correct per ticket scope (navigation-only), but the description is factually inaccurate and will mislead operators. No spec artifact was available so acceptance criteria were not independently audited (no-spec degradation). Both commit subjects follow the documented EPMCDME-####: format. Blind lens found no issues.

findings.problem: The SCHEDULERS description in both customer_config_declarations.py and customer-config.yaml says 'Schedulers navigation item and REST API for listing, toggling, and viewing run history.' This implies the flag gates API access, but the schedulers router has no feature-flag guard — the API remains accessible regardless of the flag value.
findings.impact: Operators reading the admin config UI or the YAML will believe disabling this flag also disables the REST API. It does not. This creates operational confusion and incorrect runbook assumptions.
findings.recommendation: Change the description in both places to 'Schedulers navigation item visibility — controls whether the Schedulers nav item is shown in the UI.' (The REST API is always accessible; document separately if API gating is desired in a future ticket.)

standards_review.notes: Both commits use 'EPMCDME-15013: <Description>' format matching the documented convention.
No new source files created; additions are to existing files with headers already present.
New Python constant follows existing SettingDeclaration pattern exactly. No style deviations.
